The Cross-Border Threat Detection and Supply Chain Defense (CBTS) Center of Excellence
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) proposes the establishment of the Cross-Border Threat Screening and Supply Chain Defense (CBTS) as a Center of Excellence of the
Department of Homeland Security. In support, the vision of the CBTS COE at UTRGV is to be on the cutting edge of research and function at the frontline of operations that support the mission of the DHS by promoting and carrying out impactful and relevant research through a coalition of partners committed to homeland security. The center is committed to developing products, processes, and programs that comply with the needs and demands of DHS.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements
Consortium of Advanced Additive Manufacturing Research and Education for Energy Related Systems (CA2REERs)
CONGRANT.SPONORG: DOE/NNSA: National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) Minority Serving Institutions (MSI) Program
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The goal of this project is to develop and sustain the DOE Consortium of Advanced Additive Manufacturing Research and Education for Energy Related Systems (DOE CA2REERs) to expose, recruit, engage and train students from underrepresented groups for a career in Advanced Manufacturing for Energy, following a collaborative approach by a team of investigators from 3 MSI institutions and 2 DOE Labs. The minority serving education institutions include: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (90% Hispanic), University Texas San Antonio (54% Hispanic), and University of Arizona (30% minority). The DOE/NNSA labs are Oak Ridge National Lab and Los Alamos National Lab. The consortium covers minority communities at three minority serving institutions with a total student enrollment of around 100,000 (UTRGV 27,708, UTSA 32,101, and University of Arizona 44,831). The long-term vision of the consortium is to cultivate an innovation driven manufacturing education ecosystem for Energy Innovation with programs designed to recruit young talents and prepare them with solid education and real-life experiences in energy innovation and advanced manufacturing technologies. Upon graduation, students are ready for a dream career in DOE/NNSA labs and energy industries.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Proposal to Establish a National Center for Integrated Transportation Infrastructure 4.0: Improving the Durability and Extending the Life of Transportation Infrastructure
CONGRANT.SPONORG: U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) UTC Program
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
This proposal establishes the Center for Integrated Transportation Infrastructure 4.0 (CITI-4.0), a National University Transportation Center focusing on “Improving the Durability and Extending the Life of Transportation Infrastructure”. CITI 4.0 is a consortium of seven US higher education and research institutions that consolidate their expertise, facilities, resources, and institutional support to achieve the common goals of the center. The center addresses the challenges of the new era Intelligent Transportation System in ways never previously imagined by adapting the “Industry 4.0” principles to the integrated transportation infrastructure. CITI-4.0 introduces automation, cyber-physical fusion and information driven practices, enabled by real-time data communications among heterogeneous monitoring sensors and integrates the assessment, management and maintenance activities of the infrastructure, resources and operations across railways, roadways, and ports following a data-driven performance-based approach.

Motives: North America’s demand for safe, affordable, and environmentally responsible transportation of people and goods by railway, roadway, and ports is projected to grow substantially in the years ahead. Asset managers are consistently challenged to improve the performance of the transportation network, optimize efficiency of operations and ensure safety by maximizing accessibility and reliability of the transportation infrastructure. Although accurate monitoring is a key enabler for effective operations and maintenance, the condition assessment is currently conducted based mainly on periodic, labor-intensive and time-consuming scheduled activities. The interpretation of the collected data and integration with operations is extensively dependent on the experience of the operators and other human factors. Each transportation mode relies typically on its own operations, infrastructure, and resources to meet the current network demand. These three elements are often loosely integrated within each mode, are rarely integrated across modes, and are not effectively engaged with the end users of the network.

Topic Areas: The center activities cover the following non-exclusive topics: (1) Application of new materials and technologies; (2) Cyber and communications security; (3) Condition monitoring, remote sensing, and the use of GPS; (4) Asset and performance management through data accessibility, data security and analytical tools;

Impacts: CITI-4.0 brings the infrastructure of the major transportation modes into the Industry 4.0 era as essential parts of the grand Intelligent Transportation System. The proposed CITI-4.0 research, education, workforce development, technology transfer, and diversity activities advance technology in transportation engineering and enable students and professionals from diverse socioeconomic groups throughout the country to develop the skills necessary to overcome the transportation challenges of the next era and create the next generation of worldwide leaders. This initiative benefits all stakeholders in the transportation industry, administration and legislation and sets the framework for addressing similar problems around the world.

CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The purpose of this work is to establish a real time productivity monitoring and management system. This system will be based on enhanced productivity measurement and control tools providing an extended work science tool kit. CONGRANT.TITLE: Talent Development for Smart Manufacturing
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This proposed effort will 1) develop and offer a summer certificate program for executives, engineers and undergraduate students with a focus on smart manufacturing science and technology; and 2) develop a Master of Science in Manufacturing Engineering with concentration in smart manufacturing and manufacturing analytics. These two programs are proposed recognizing the needs for talents required to drive innovation in smart manufacturing. It aims to prepare students/professionals with multidisciplinary knowledge and research experiences in related fields, which is not readily provided within existing traditional engineering programs. These two talent development programs prepare students with theories and tools in information collection and modeling, sensor, robotics, data mining, data analytics and science, artificial intelligence, systems, and decision models which can be used to monitor, predict, control and improve the behavior and performance of materials, structures, products, processes, services, and systems ranging from micro-scale to macro-scale. Students in MS program will conduct multidisciplinary research related to smart technologies or lead innovation in manufacturing industries.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Development of a Small-Business Data Management Pull System; A Case Study

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: UTRGV

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the IISE Annual Conference & Expo 2023
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Babski-Reeves, B. Eksioglu, D. Hampton
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to the U.S. Small Business Association, small businesses of five hundred employees or fewer make up 99.9% of all U.S. businesses [1]. However, 65% of new businesses fail within the first ten years of opening, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This case study will center around the used vehicle market, where small businesses that focus on buying and selling used cars have had issues with accurately tracking information due to the lack of a proper data-entry system. Despite the common use of a car, no thorough study has been done to develop or build an information tracking system at a small scale. Many companies lack a proper data management system to adequately manage the documentation of inventory. This lack of structure is costing companies money along with constant errors going undetected when inputting information. The tracker will be done in Excel, due to the widespread usage in small businesses. The manual data will be digitized and will keep track of inventory on hand. Using advanced functions and formulas in excel, the information tracker will be able to display necessary information for easy analysis. This system will use dynamic ranges for summations of expenses, dynamic tables, and dynamic XLOOKUP functions to allow the user to easily input data while minimizing the potential errors and creating an easy-to-read table of inventory. The expected result is to develop a simple information tracking system that allows the user to input all data necessary in small business applications.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A Study of Human Balance and Coordination Using a Head Mounted Display

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Journal of Computers and Information Science in Engineering
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper investigates the hypothesis that men and women perform differently in virtual environments in terms of balance and coordination during surprise events. It reports on an experiment in human subject balance and coordination using an HTC Vive head-mounted display (HMD) to create a virtual environment. For the experiment, 30 male and 30 female subjects of college age were asked to navigate along a clear path in a virtual world using a controller with their dominant hand and asked to balance a virtual ball on a virtual plate using the other controller in the nondominant hand. The test subjects moved along a clearly marked path, with three surprise obstacles occurring: a large rock landing near the path, an explosion near the path, and a flock of birds coming across the path. Data included six degrees-of-freedom (DOF) trajectories for the head and both hands, as well as data gathered by the computer system on ball location and velocity, plate location and velocity, and ball status. Likert scale questionnaires were answered by the test subjects relative to video game experience, sense of presence, and ease of managing the ball movement. Statistics showed that the male students dropped the ball less frequently at p = 0.0254 and p = 0.0036. In contrast, female students were aware of their performance with correlation levels of 0.632 and 0.588.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Assessing the Feasibility of a Biofilter in Medium-to-High Scale Industries

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: UTRGV

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the 2020 IISE Annual Conference
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The removal of volatile organic compounds, VOCs, from contaminated sources of air stream has become a major air pollution risk. Excessive amounts discharged to the atmosphere are highly risky to human health and to the environmental system. Demand for sustainable VOC control technologies has become crucial to ensure the reduction of emissions. Biological treatments of waste gas streams, such as biofiltration, have proven to be cost effective and environmentally friendly compared to conventional pollution control technologies. Yet, only a few studies on medium scale biofilters have been conducted before. In order to evaluate the optimal design of medium scale biofilters for treatment, the goal of this research is to simulate data for a given biofilter model, and to evaluate if it is economically and environmentally feasible to implement with a given set of conditions based on previous data. The model incorporates key parameters such as annual capital costs, investment costs, and annual operating costs. Results and observations are reported to show promise for developing a model that can routinely and reliable describe the effectiveness of a biofiltration system for medium scale industries.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Risk Factor Simulation and Cost Estimation of Undiagnosed High Blood Pressure in Young Adults

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: UTRGV

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: IIE Transactions on Healthcare System Engineering
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Current estimates for health costs are wide ranging to non-existent, yet they play a key role on the culture of preventive care, making early detection of asymptomatic conditions like high blood pressure (HBP) a challenge. To address this, a risk factor simulation model and annual expected cost function were developed to determine the annual expected cost of medical complications associated to misdiagnosis of HBP in young adults. The designed simulation estimated the likelihood of misdiagnosis for pre-hypertension, stage 1, and stage 2 hypertension in young males and females of different races/ethnicities. This estimate was included in an expected cost function to compute the individual economic impact. The models found that, at the national level, 60.53% of men and 59.72% of women ages 18 to 24 are at risk of misdiagnosis and could incur on individual annual expenses of up to $63,000 depending on the degree of their condition. The study also evaluated a case study of the South Texas population where the adjusted models estimated that about 62.64% of men and 61.72% of women are at risk of uncontrolled HBP due to lack of diagnosis and are expected to spend about the same as the nation to deal with complications of HBP.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/MTT Risk Factor Simulation and Cost Estimation Rev-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Annual Expected Cost of High Blood Pressure in Young Adults

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: UTRGV
UTRGV
UTRGV

INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Coperich, E. Cudney, and H. Nembhard
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Medical costs estimates are wide ranging or non-existent, yet they can influence preventive care, in particular asymptomatic conditions like high blood pressure (HBP).  To address this, a simulation model and expected cost function were developed to determine the annual expected cost of medical complications associated to misdiagnosis of HBP in young adults. According to the American Heart Association, adults 18 to 24 years old are 28% less likely of being diagnosed with HBP on regular medical visits compared to those 60 or older. The simulation estimated the average risk factor of false negatives in HBP diagnosis for young adults nationally. This estimate was included in the cost function to compute the individual economic impact. The models found that, at the national level, close to 40% of individuals is at risk of misdiagnosis and individual annual expenses could reach almost $92,000. This should motivate early-age blood pressure monitoring in order to preserve the physical and economic integrity of the young adult population. The study also evaluated a case study of the South Texas population where the adjusted models estimated that about 25% of young adults are at high risk of HBP and annual expected costs for misdiagnosed individuals was close to $100,000.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Modeling and optimization of the molten salt cleaning process

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas - Pan American

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Molten salt cleaning is a very efficient and effective cleaning method for removing paints, oils and greases, ceramics, and oxide scales from the surface of metal substrates. Although this cleaning method has been used for decades, very limited research work can be found in literature to help remanufacturers in process modeling and parameter optimization. In order to fill the gap, the effects of molten salt on different types of metal substrates are investigated. The impact on the hardness and tensile strength of the substrates is studied. The relationship between the cleaning performances and processing parameters including salt ingredients and temperature, are explored. Finally, mathematical models are suggested to provide remanufacturers directions in selection of the optimal parameters for the molten salt cleaning process.
